name: WinaltChat for WooCommerce
author: Winalt Technologies

sections.description:
WinaltChat adds a fast, intelligent chat widget to your
WooCommerce store. Customers can search your product catalogue,
get instant answers about shipping and returns, and — when they
need a real person — connect to your support team through a built-in
live chat system, all without leaving your store.

AI Shopping Assistant

  • Dual AI Modes — Use your own API key from Groq — LLaMA
    (Free Tier), ChatGPT (OpenAI), Claude (Anthropic), or Gemini
    (Google) for full conversational AI. No key? The built-in
    Basic AI mode runs entirely on your server with zero external
    calls and zero ongoing cost.
  • Smart Product Search — Intent-aware search across your
    WooCommerce catalogue. Handles typos, synonyms, multilingual and mixed-language
    queries, and follow-up questions naturally.
  • Product Comparisons — Customers can ask “which is better, the Sony or the
    Samsung?” and get a clear side-by-side comparison
    with prices and key specs from your own catalogue.
  • Store Knowledge Base — Reads your shipping, returns, contact,
    and about pages to answer policy questions accurately and
    dynamically — no hardcoded answers that break for other stores.
  • Conversation Context — Remembers context within a session so
    follow-up questions (“does it come in blue?”) work naturally.
  • Amazon Affiliate Fallback — When a product is out of stock,
    optionally suggest an Amazon affiliate link so you still earn a
    commission.

Live Human Chat

  • Human Handoff — When a customer types phrases like “I want
    to talk to a human”, “customer service”, “live agent”, or dozens
    of natural variants, the plugin detects the request and connects
    them to a real person on your team.
  • Admin Live Chats Dashboard — A dedicated Live Chats screen
    in your WordPress admin shows all active, waiting, and closed
    conversations in a two-panel interface. Keep the tab open to stay
    marked online for visitors.
  • Visitor Name Prompt — Before connecting, the visitor is
    optionally asked for their name. If skipped, they are identified
    as “Visitor #ID” so you can tell conversations apart.
  • Full Conversation Context for Agents — When a customer is
    handed off, the admin sees the complete prior AI conversation so
    there is no need to ask “how can I help?” twice.
  • Visitor Presence Dot — A green dot shows the visitor is
    active. It turns grey within 30 seconds if they close the tab.
  • Two-Tier Timeout — If your team does not respond within
    90 seconds, the visitor sees a friendly patience message. After
    5 minutes of no reply, the chat gracefully falls back to the AI
    assistant with an optional email capture.
  • Intelligent Offline Handling — When no admin is online the AI
    keeps helping. Visitors can optionally leave their email for a
    follow-up. Leads appear in the admin Live Chats list with a
    dedicated Leads section and unread badge.
  • Session Management — Close chats when resolved, or delete
    them permanently. Closed and lead sessions stay visible in
    their own sections until manually removed.
  • Zero External Dependencies — Live chat runs entirely within
    your WordPress site using secure AJAX polling over the REST API.
    No Pusher, no third-party service, no extra cost.
  • Email Notifications — Get an email when a customer starts a
    live chat or leaves their contact details while you are offline.

Privacy & Security

  • All live chat data is stored in your own WordPress database.
    Nothing is sent to an external service.
  • Session tokens are 32-character cryptographically random strings
    — not sequential IDs — so sessions cannot be enumerated.
  • All endpoints enforce nonces, capability checks, input
    sanitization, output escaping, and rate limiting.
  • Message content is sanitized server-side, and rich chat HTML
    (product cards, links, images) is additionally sanitized
    client-side via a bundled copy of DOMPurify before being
    rendered — see “Bundled Libraries” below.

Bundled Libraries

  • DOMPurify 3.1.6 — client-side HTML sanitizer, used to safely
    render rich chat content (product cards, links, images).
    Vendored locally at assets/js/vendor/purify.min.js; not loaded
    from a CDN. © Cure53 and other contributors. Dual-licensed under
    the Apache License 2.0 and Mozilla Public License 2.0, both
    GPL-compatible. github.com/cure53/DOMPurify

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.2 or later
  • WooCommerce 7.0 or later (must be installed and active)
  • PHP 7.4 or later
  • An API key from Groq, OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google (optional —
    Basic AI and Live Chat both work without one)

Support

  • Support Forum: wordpress.org/support/plugin/winaltchat-for-woocommerce
  • Email: support@winalttechnologies.com

We aim to respond to all support requests within 48 hours.

External Services

This plugin connects to third-party AI providers only when you
configure an external AI mode and enter your own API key. In Basic
AI mode and during live human chat, no external AI service is used.

AI Providers (optional — only when an API key is configured)

Customer messages, recent conversation context, and relevant store
and product context are sent to the AI provider you select so it
can generate a response. No data is sent to these providers when
using Basic AI mode.

  • Groq — groq.com | Privacy Policy | Terms of Service
  • OpenAI — openai.com | Privacy Policy | Terms of Use
  • Anthropic Claude — anthropic.com | Privacy Policy | Terms of Service
  • Google Gemini — ai.google.dev | Privacy Policy | Terms of Service

Amazon Associate Program (optional — only when a tag is configured)

When the Amazon fallback is enabled and no matching product is
found in your store, the plugin generates an Amazon search link
with your Associate tag. No customer data is transmitted to Amazon
by the plugin — the link simply directs the visitor’s browser.

  • Amazon — amazon.com | Privacy Notice

Deactivation Feedback (optional — only sent if you respond to the deactivation survey)

When you deactivate this plugin, an optional short survey asks why.
If you respond (or skip), your site URL, the plugin/WordPress/PHP
version, and whatever you entered in the survey are sent to
Winalt Technologies to help improve the plugin. No personal data is
collected beyond this unless you choose to type it into the free-text
field yourself.

  • Winalt Technologies — aisalesmanchatpro.com | Privacy Policy

Anonymous Usage Tracking (optional — off by default, only sent if you click “Allow”)

On first use, a notice asks permission to send anonymous “still
active” pings to help us understand real-world installs. Nothing is
sent unless you click “Allow” — you can also decline, or change your
choice later from the plugin’s General Settings tab. When enabled,
your site URL and the plugin/WordPress/PHP version are sent to Winalt
Technologies once immediately and then roughly once a day for as long
as it stays enabled. No personal or customer data is ever included.

  • Winalt Technologies — aisalesmanchatpro.com | Privacy Policy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the winaltchat-for-woocommerce folder to
    /wp-content/plugins/, or install directly via the WordPress
    Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Make sure WooCommerce is installed and active.
  4. Navigate to WinaltChat → Settings in the WordPress admin.
  5. AI Mode (optional): Choose your preferred AI provider and
    enter your API key, or leave blank to use the built-in Basic AI
    mode at zero cost.
  6. Live Human Chat (optional): Scroll to the Live Human Chat
    section, enable the toggle, set a notification email and agent
    display name. A Live Chats item will appear in the sidebar.
  7. Keep the Live Chats tab open in your browser while you work
    to appear online to visitors requesting a human.
  8. Customise the chat appearance under the Chat Appearance tab.
sections.faq:
Do I need an API key to use this plugin?

No. The built-in Basic AI mode handles product search, comparisons,
policy questions, and conversation without any API key or external
service. Real AI mode (Groq, OpenAI, Claude, Gemini) is optional
and improves response quality for complex queries.

Does Live Human Chat require any external service?

No. It runs entirely within your WordPress site using the WordPress
REST API. No Pusher, no LiveChat subscription, no third-party
accounts needed.

How does the admin know a customer is waiting?

Two ways: a browser notification fires in the Live Chats tab (if
you grant notification permission), and an email is sent to your
configured notify address. Keep the Live Chats tab open while
you work to stay marked as online.

What happens if no admin is online when a customer asks for help?

The AI assistant keeps helping the customer seamlessly. A message
explains the team is unavailable, and the customer is offered an
optional email field so you can follow up. No dead ends.

How long before an unanswered live chat falls back to the AI?

At 90 seconds of no response, the visitor sees a friendly
“thanks for your patience” message. At 5 minutes, the chat
gracefully returns to AI mode with an email capture option. Both
thresholds are configurable in the Live Human Chat settings.

Can multiple admins handle chats at the same time?

Currently any admin with the manage_options capability can see and
reply to all live chats. Multi-agent role management is planned for
a future release.

How do I remove all plugin data on uninstall?

Deleting the plugin via the WordPress Plugins screen automatically
removes all WinaltChat settings, options, and live chat database
tables from your site.

Does it work with my theme?

Yes. The chat widget is injected into the page footer and uses its
own scoped CSS so it does not conflict with theme styles.

Will it slow down my site?

The AI chat widget loads asynchronously and does not block page
rendering. Live chat polling only runs while an active live session
is in progress — normal AI chat and idle pages make zero polling
requests.
sections.changelog:
1.17.2

  • Fix: “Show me toys” confidently returned an unrelated pet product (“Dog Chew Toy Bundle”) instead of the actual toy products. normalize_keyword() singularizes a query keyword (“toys” -> “toy”) but the title/category text being matched against was never singularized, so a plural category like “Toys” could never match a strict \btoy\b word-boundary pattern while a product with the literal word “Toy” in its title won by default. The matching pattern now allows an optional trailing “s”/”es”.
  • Fix: Multi-item comparisons (“compare the laptop, TV, and camera”) were phrasing-dependent — a generic single-word name like “laptop” could return an accessory (“Laptop Backpack”) instead of the real product, because a tied keyword-overlap score fell back to whichever candidate sorted first by price rather than any relevance signal; and an item could silently vanish from the comparison with no explanation if its best match happened to coincide with an earlier item’s. Ties are now broken by weighting a product-category match higher than a bare title substring, and a name whose best match is already claimed by an earlier comparison item now falls back to its own next-best candidate instead of being dropped. Multi-word names (e.g. “13-inch laptop”) also now retry as individual keywords if the exact-phrase search finds nothing.
  • Fix: Sending a chat message that was only <script>alert('xss')</script> returned a generic “Sorry, there was an error processing your request.” (HTTP 400) — no script ever executed (this was a stability bug, not a security one), but WordPress core’s sanitizer deletes a <script>/<style> tag’s entire contents, not just the markup, so an all-script-tag message sanitized down to an empty string and tripped the “please provide a message” check. The message sanitizer now falls back to angle-bracket-escaping instead of stripping when that would otherwise wipe out non-empty input, so it’s treated like any other odd chat message and gets a normal response.

1.17.1

  • Improve: The usage-tracking opt-in notice rendered via WordPress core’s admin_notices hook, which shows above any page’s own custom UI — so it appeared above the plugin’s topbar/tabs instead of inside the dashboard. Now rendered directly inside the dashboard, below the tabs, styled as a card matching the rest of the page instead of a generic WordPress notice.

1.17.0

  • New: Added opt-in anonymous usage tracking. A one-time admin notice asks permission to send anonymous “still active” pings (site URL, WordPress/PHP/plugin version — no personal or customer data); off by default until you click “Allow”, and a toggle on the General Settings tab lets you change your choice at any time. Disclosed under “External Services” in this readme.

1.16.1

  • Improve: Dropped the 🚀 emoji from the “Upgrade to Pro” submenu item and styled its label as a pill (same colors as the topbar badge) instead, so it reads as a button rather than plain text in the WordPress admin sidebar. Styled with inline CSS rather than a shared class, since this menu item renders on every wp-admin screen but the plugin’s stylesheet only loads on its own pages.

1.16.0

  • New: Added a permanent “Upgrade to Pro” admin menu item and a persistent topbar badge, both free-tier only (hidden automatically once winalt_is_pro() returns true). Clicking either opens a simple in-admin page listing the genuine current WinaltChat Pro features — unlimited agents/quick replies/pinned conversations, the Tracking/Analytics Dashboard, Weekly Email Reports, and AI response feedback tools — with an “Upgrade Now” button linking out to the Pro site (tagged utm_medium=admin_menu / utm_campaign=permanent_upgrade_link so it’s distinguishable from other upgrade prompts in analytics).

1.15.20

  • Fix: “do you sell bicycles?” still found nothing even after last round’s category-taxonomy search fix, because the product is titled “Mountain Bike 21-Speed” and categorized “Bikes” — neither contains the literal substring “bicycle”, and no amount of plural/singular stemming turns “bicycles” into “bike”. Added an explicit, curated synonym (bicycle/bicycles -> bike) checked in both the Basic AI and Real AI search paths; “do you have a mountain bike?” already worked, confirming this was purely a wording gap.
  • Fix: category/tag taxonomy search used hide_empty => true when looking up matching terms, which relies on each term’s cached product count — a count that can go stale (e.g. a tag added via quick-edit, import, or anything that skips a term-count recalculation) and silently hide a term with real products assigned to it, even for an exact literal match. Changed to hide_empty => false; the follow-up query already does its own live per-term lookup, so a genuinely empty term still returns nothing — this only gains recall, never loses precision.

1.15.19

  • Security: Pinned brace-expansion (transitive dev dependency of the Playwright E2E test suite, via minimatch/@wordpress/env) to 2.1.4 via an npm overrides entry in tests/e2e/package.json, patching GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (CVE-2026-14257) — versions before 2.1.3 bounded the count of brace-expansion results but not their length, so a ~7.5KB crafted input could grow output unboundedly and crash the Node process with an out-of-memory error. Dev/test-only tooling dependency, never shipped to production sites.

1.15.18

  • Fix: “Security Scan” CI was failing on main since 1.15.15 — a docblock’s long description started with a lowercase method-name reference (search_products_by_query()...), which PHPCS’s WordPress-Extra ruleset flags as a blocking error. Reworded to start with a capital letter; no logic change.
  • Security: Updated composer.lock to pull in wp-coding-standards/wpcs 3.4.1, patching GHSA-3pwp-g2mj-5p3v (CVE-2026-45293) — versions before 3.4.1 ran a scanned function argument through eval() while checking for a falsy value, so a maliciously crafted argument could execute arbitrary code during a PHPCS run. Dev-only dependency (require-dev), never shipped to production sites; composer.json‘s existing ^3.3 constraint already permitted this version.

1.15.17

  • Fix: “Add to Cart” from the chat widget added the item correctly but navigated the whole tab to the site homepage/blog (?add-to-cart=ID on home_url('/')) with no visible success confirmation. Now navigates to the actual cart page instead, matching the pattern already used by the purchase-intent flow, so the customer lands somewhere that unambiguously shows the item was added.
  • Fix: Comparing 3+ products at once (“compare the laptop, the TV, and the camera”, “what’s the difference between X, Y, and Z”) either returned an irrelevant response or silently dropped all but one of the requested products. The comparison parser only ever extracted exactly two product names via a single regex; a third name got swallowed into the first as one garbled string. Rewrote extraction to split Oxford-comma/”and”/”vs” lists into N names and made the comparison handler loop over all of them; two-item comparisons are unaffected.
  • Fix: Plural product searches (“show me laptops”) could return “we don’t carry that” and only surface an unrelated accessory (e.g. a laptop backpack whose description happened to mention “laptops”), while the exact in-stock product (“13-inch Laptop”) was left out — because the literal-to-singular retry in Real AI’s product-context search only ran when the literal plural query found zero results, and a coincidental partial match blocked it from ever firing. The singular-form retry now always runs and merges in, regardless of whether the literal query already matched something else.

1.15.16

  • Fix: “How do I checkout?” and similar checkout-process questions fell through intent detection as ‘unknown’, which the hybrid REST router treats as a passthrough — spending a paid Real AI API call on a question Basic AI’s own payment-info responder (real WooCommerce gateway list) could answer directly. Added “checkout” to the payment information-intent keywords.

1.15.15

  • Fix: Real AI mode falsely denied carrying entire categories it genuinely stocks — “do you sell bicycles?”, “show me books”, “show me sports equipment”, and “show me toys” all returned “not carried” or an incomplete/wrong result, while specific product names (“mountain bike”, exact titles) worked fine. Real AI’s product search only ever checked title/content text, never a product’s assigned category. Added category/tag/brand taxonomy search, matching what Basic AI already does.

1.15.14

  • Fix: The “View Full Product Page” / “View Product” link shown in product-image and product-detail responses never carried a data-product-id attribute, so a click on it always resolved to product_id = 0 instead of the real product — breaking contextual comparison lookups (which match on data-product-id) for the product shown. Fixed in all four locations that render this link.

1.15.13

  • Fix: Basic AI gift/occasion queries like “birthday gift idea for my dad who loves cooking” searched on literal filler words (“birthday”, “gift”, “idea”) instead of the actual interest (“cooking”) — Basic AI’s own keyword extractor had the same gap already fixed for Real AI. Also added a gerund-stripping retry (“cooking” -> “cook”) so the extracted interest can match a title like “Slow Cooker”.

1.15.12

  • Fix: The “More like this” quick-reply chip returned completely unrelated products (e.g. a Mountain Bike and Washing Machine “similar to” a Digital Mirrorless Camera) — it searched WordPress full-text for the entire previous message verbatim (e.g. “Tell me about the Digital Mirrorless Camera”) instead of extracting real keywords first, so common filler words (“tell”, “me”, “about”, “the”) matched unrelated product titles/descriptions almost at random. Now runs through the same keyword extraction as every other search.
  • Fix: Asking about a genuinely out-of-catalogue product (e.g. “Do you sell drones?”) could return a nonsensical “closest alternative” (a Dog Chew Toy Bundle for a drone question, a random TV for a PS5 question) — a fallback meant only for empty/no-specific-query cases was incorrectly also firing whenever a specific, unmatched product query came up empty, handing the AI an arbitrary alphabetical slice of the catalogue as its “STORE INVENTORY” context. That fallback is now scoped to genuinely empty queries only, and the AI is instructed not to force an unrelated substitute when nothing relevant is actually available.

1.15.11

  • Improve: Chat requests occasionally hit a dead-end error requiring a manual page reload when a CDN/WAF in front of the site (e.g. Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode or rate limiting) intercepted a request before it reached this plugin’s REST endpoint. The widget now recognizes this specific failure shape (a non-JSON error body — our own /chat endpoint always returns JSON, even on its own errors) and automatically retries once after a short delay before showing any error, with a friendlier fallback message if the retry also fails.

1.15.10

  • Fix: Real AI mode falsely claimed the store carries no watches (“show me watches” returned “we do not currently carry watches”) even though a Men’s Leather Watch and Fitness Smartwatch exist — the product-context search used a literal WP substring match that never matched “watches” against “Watch”/”Smartwatch”. Added plural- and gerund-aware retry passes (watches→watch, appliances→appliance, gardening→garden) shared with Basic AI’s keyword normalizer.
  • Fix: Raw internal “ID:66, ID:15, …” inventory text occasionally leaked straight into the visible chat reply instead of rendering as product cards. Added a defensive strip of any leaked “ID:NNN” tokens from the final AI response, matching the existing price-hallucination cleanup pattern.
  • Fix: Gift/occasion queries like “birthday gift idea for my dad who loves gardening” pulled in irrelevant products (Birthday Balloon Garland Kit, etc.) because filler words (“birthday”, “gift”, “idea”, “dad”, “loves”) were treated as literal search keywords. Expanded the Real AI stop-word list to filter gift/occasion/relationship framing words so only the actual interest (“gardening”) is searched.

1.15.9

  • Fix: “Do you sell a PlayStation 5?” generated an Amazon fallback search for “a playstation 5” instead of “playstation 5” — the phrase-removal step only strips known fixed phrases like “do you sell”, leaving an orphaned leading article dangling in front of the actual product name. Now stripped as a separate step.

1.15.8

  • Fix: “Kitchen appliances” returned a product that isn’t in the store’s actual “Kitchen Appliances” category — it was matched via a generic “Appliances” category and an unrelated “Home & Kitchen” parent category (matched only because its name happens to contain the word “kitchen”), pulled in independently by each half of the query. Multi-word category-style queries now try the full phrase against category names first, and use the specific category it finds (e.g. “Kitchen Appliances” itself) instead of unioning both words’ independent, looser matches.

1.15.7

  • Fix: “Show me watches” only returned “Men’s Leather Watch” — a “Fitness Smartwatch” in the same catalogue was silently excluded because the title-match check required “watch” as a whole word, and “smartwatch” has no word boundary between “smart” and “watch” for it to match against. Keywords of 4+ characters now also match as the tail end of a compound word (e.g. “watch” now matches “smartwatch”, “phone” now matches “headphone”), while staying strict for short keywords so something like “arm” still can’t match inside an unrelated word like “alarm”.

1.15.6

  • Improve: Removed the extra text box that appeared when selecting “Other” on the deactivation feedback survey — redundant with the existing free-text comments field already on the same form.

1.15.5

  • Fix: “I’m ready to buy the 13-inch laptop, how do I purchase it?” returned ordering instructions for a completely different product (whatever was last shown in the conversation, e.g. from an earlier comparison) instead of the laptop actually named in the message. The purchase-intent handler only ever looked at conversation context for a product, never at what the current message itself named — now it parses the product name out of the message first, only falling back to context for pronoun-only phrasing like “I’ll take it”.
  • Fix: The typo-correction feature could rewrite a correctly-spelled word into an unrelated, real product-title word purely from character similarity — e.g. “I want something to help me relax and sleep better at night” got “night” “corrected” to “light” (an 80% character match), returning five irrelevant light-themed products instead of nothing. Phonetic similarity (soundex) is now a required check, not just a bonus score — “night” and “light” are phonetically distinct, while genuine typos like “laptp”→”laptop” still correct correctly.

1.15.4

  • Fix: Submitting the deactivation feedback survey returned a 400 error in the browser console and never actually recorded anything — the JS sent action=winaltchat_deactivation_feedback but the PHP handler was registered under wp_ajax_winalt_deactivation_feedback (missing “chat”), a mismatch WordPress core silently 400s on with no indication why. Corrected, and the action name (along with the nonce action) is now defined once in PHP and passed to JS, rather than duplicated as separate literal strings in two files.

1.15.3

  • Fix: Clicking “Send & Deactivate” without selecting a reason silently behaved like “Skip & Deactivate” — nothing was sent, with no indication why. Now requires a reason to be selected before sending, showing an inline message pointing at “Skip & Deactivate” as the always-available no-friction alternative; deactivation is still never blocked or delayed by this.

1.15.2

  • Fix: The deactivation feedback request (added in 1.15.0) sent a payload shape the receiving endpoint didn’t actually accept — it checks for a feedback_type field (not type) and has a single free-text details column rather than separate reason/comments/site/version fields, so every submission was being silently rejected. Payload corrected to match the endpoint’s real format; behavior is otherwise unchanged (still nonce-checked, still never blocks or slows down deactivation, still fails silently on any error).
  • Docs: Disclosed the deactivation-feedback endpoint under “External Services” in this readme.

1.15.1

  • Fix: The deactivation feedback modal (added in 1.15.0) could be silently closed within a few seconds by another active plugin’s own “auto-dismiss popups” script on the Plugins page — a real risk on stores running many plugins, since such scripts commonly target any element that looks like a modal/overlay by class name or ARIA role. Rendered inside a Shadow DOM now, making it unreachable to any other script on the page regardless of what it’s matching against.

1.15.0

  • Feature: A short, optional feedback survey now appears when deactivating the plugin from the Plugins page, asking why (with an “Other” free-text option and an optional comments field). Deactivation always proceeds regardless of whether feedback is sent or skipped, and never waits more than 2 seconds on the network. No personal data is collected beyond the site URL, unless voluntarily typed into the free-text fields.

1.14.16

  • Fix: The chat message endpoint required a WordPress REST nonce, which is tied to the visitor’s session/cookie state — any caching layer (full-page cache, CDN, object cache) that serves a page slightly out of sync with a visitor’s actual session could desync it, returning “Sorry, there was an error processing your request” (403 rest_cookie_invalid_nonce), worse for anyone logged in. This endpoint doesn’t write anything server-side (message + client-supplied history in, an AI response out), so there’s nothing a nonce meaningfully protects here — removed the nonce requirement entirely and rely solely on the existing IP-based rate limiter for abuse control, which doesn’t depend on cookies/sessions and is unaffected by caching.

1.14.15

  • Fix: The auto-refreshing nonce endpoint (/nonce) was a GET request. A Cache-Control: no-store response header only asks a cache to behave — it can’t force a CDN, reverse proxy, or “cache everything” rule to honor it, so on some hosting setups this endpoint kept handing back a stale, cached nonce every time, and the 403 it exists to prevent (surfaced to visitors as “Sorry, there was an error processing your request”) never actually cleared. Switched to POST, which no HTTP cache stores by default regardless of configuration, so this no longer depends on the hosting layer behaving correctly.

1.14.14

  • Improve: Applied WordPress Coding Standards (WPCS) formatting across the codebase — the ruleset was declared in phpcs.xml from day one but never actually enforced in CI, so formatting drift (indentation, quote style, array formatting) accumulated over time. Fixed mechanically via phpcbf plus 31 missing function docblocks added by hand. No functional changes: verified via php -l on every touched file, manual review of every non-whitespace diff, and the existing PHP regression suite (all 51 tests still pass). This is what unblocks the new PHPCS CI gate from failing on unrelated pre-existing debt.

1.14.13

  • Version bump only, to force a fresh asset download (new ?ver= cache-busting query string on every enqueued script/style) for sites where a CDN or browser had the pre-1.14.12 JS cached. No code changes since 1.14.12.

1.14.12

  • Fix: The nonce-auto-refresh module (chat-config.js) never actually fired its on-page-load request, defeating the whole reason it exists (surviving a stale nonce baked into full-page-cached HTML). Its localized config data was attached to the entry-point script (winaltchat-chat-core) instead of the config module itself (winaltchat-chat-config), which loads and runs earlier in the dependency chain — so the refresh call always ran before window.winaltConfig existed and silently no-op’d. Now localized directly onto winaltchat-chat-config so the data is available before that module’s own code runs.

1.14.11

  • Fix: A follow-up question about products just shown (e.g. “show me cameras” then “which one is cheaper?”) ignored the two cameras on screen and instead returned six unrelated store-wide cheapest items. The bare word “cheaper” in the message matched the generic cheapest-items handler before the contextual comparison check got a chance to run, because that check’s phrase list only covered quality comparisons (“which is better”) and not price ones. Now “which one is cheaper/more expensive” correctly compares the products already shown.

1.14.10

  • Fix: A vague/semantic shopping query containing the word “help” anywhere in it (e.g. “I want something to help me relax and sleep better at night”) was misclassified as a “what can you do” capabilities request instead of a product search — the AI answered with its own generic capabilities blurb instead of searching for relax/sleep products. The help-intent word list matched bare “help” unconditionally and outranked the product-search match; now “help me ” is recognized as a task/product request instead.

1.14.9

  • Fix: The internal RELEASE_PROCESS.md dev doc was synced to the WordPress.org SVN trunk on the previous deploy because .distignore didn’t list it. Now excluded; this release re-syncs trunk to drop it.

1.14.8

  • Fix: A single-product result (e.g. “Do you have dress?”) could show a dangling “⭐ Popular Choice -” fragment with nothing after the dash, above the actual product intro. The default sales-tactic benefit description ended mid-sentence, relying on a conditional rating/popularity check to complete it — with neither available, it stayed incomplete and leaked straight into the response. Now always a complete, standalone sentence regardless of what data is available afterward.

1.14.7

  • Fix: “I’m looking for a food chopper for a family of 5” (where “family” happened to match a store category) answered “I couldn’t find “family i’m looking food chopper” in our store right now” — filler words like “i’m” and “looking” leaked into the search keywords and straight into that user-facing message. Caused by the 1.14.4 fix for catalog-category mentions dropping the rest of the query: it merged in the message’s other words correctly, but through a stopword list too sparse to catch ordinary filler verbs and contractions. Expanded it to match the filler words already used safely elsewhere in this plugin’s search matching.

1.14.5 – 1.14.6

  • Hardened the live-chat polling endpoints against CDN/host caching: first with stronger Cache-Control/LiteSpeed-specific headers, then by switching visitor-poll, admin-poll, and admin-sessions from GET to POST (HTTP caches never store POST by default, regardless of configuration — a structural fix, not a header). Full details on GitHub.

1.14.3 – 1.14.4

  • Fixed several product-search matching bugs from live test transcripts: “smart tv” returning any “Smart X” product, a garbled “water-bottle-1l/)” response fragment, and a catalog-category mention (“bike”) discarding the rest of the query’s keywords (“toolkit”). Full details on GitHub.

1.14.0 – 1.14.2

  • Added a “Visit plugin site” link to the Plugins list row; fixed the best-sellers fallback exposing internal store state (“we don’t have enough sales data…”) and a literal “### You Might Also Like:” heading leaking into chat responses. Full details on GitHub.

1.13.1 – 1.13.7

  • Live-chat polish following the 1.13.0 feature: fixed admin replies silently failing to reach the visitor on caching hosts/CDNs (missing nocache_headers()), fixed the name/email prompts missing the bot avatar, reworded and reordered the “agent joined” notice (now “[First name] joined the chat,” shown before their first reply, using the actual replying admin’s name), stopped the chat header from switching to the agent’s name, and fixed two mis-suppressed Plugin Check warnings. Full details on GitHub.

1.13.0

  • Feature: Proactively offers to connect the customer with live chat on product-defect complaints, service complaints/frustration, and order-status replies (when live chat is enabled), instead of only text-based “contact us” phrasing.
  • Fix: “My blender stopped working after two weeks” was treated as a fresh product search and pitched the very item that just broke — now recognized as a defect complaint and routed to support/live chat.
  • Fix: “Do you offer bulk discounts?” matched the generic discount-query keyword and showed an unrelated sale-items listing — now recognized as a bulk/wholesale enquiry and routed to the team’s contact email (and live chat, if enabled).

1.12.1 – 1.12.4

  • Several rounds of Basic AI answer-quality fixes from live test transcripts: category-priority matching (cash on delivery vs. shipping), honest shipping/returns/hours page fallbacks, gift/budget price-filter parsing, discount-query false positives, negated purchase/comparison keywords, typo-correction over-eagerness, and a fast-path crash guard. Full details on GitHub.

1.12.0

  • Feature: The “Popular products” quick-reply chip now shows genuinely popular products — ranked by real WooCommerce sales count, not the entire catalog. Falls back to average rating for stores with no sales history yet, then to newest products if there’s no rating data either, honestly labeling the response each time rather than calling something popular that isn’t. Handled directly by Basic AI, bypassing the AI provider call.

1.10.1 – 1.11.2

  • Redesigned product cards (SALE badge, ratings, standalone layout) shared between AI-provider and Basic AI paths; dynamic quick-reply chips; message avatars; “Powered by AI” header subtitle; chat-history export CSS fix; product-search/checkout-chip routing fixes; Live Chats admin console/search fixes. Full details on GitHub.

1.7.2 – 1.10.5

  • CDN-aware rate limiting, cache-safe nonce refresh, bundled-DOMPurify sanitizer consolidation, locally-bundled provider logos, translation template, various coding-standards and @since-tag fixes. Full details on GitHub.

1.7.1 and earlier

  • For the full version history, see the plugin’s GitHub repository.

short_description: WinaltChat – AI chatbot and live human chat for WooCommerce. Find products, answer questions, connect customers to your support team.
description:
WinaltChat adds a fast, intelligent chat widget to your
WooCommerce store. Customers can search your product catalogue,
get instant answers about shipping and returns, and — when they
need a real person — connect to your support team through a built-in
live chat system, all without leaving your store.

AI Shopping Assistant

  • Dual AI Modes — Use your own API key from Groq — LLaMA
    (Free Tier), ChatGPT (OpenAI), Claude (Anthropic), or Gemini
    (Google) for full conversational AI. No key? The built-in
    Basic AI mode runs entirely on your server with zero external
    calls and zero ongoing cost.
  • Smart Product Search — Intent-aware search across your
    WooCommerce catalogue. Handles typos, synonyms, multilingual and mixed-language
    queries, and follow-up questions naturally.
  • Product Comparisons — Customers can ask “which is better, the Sony or the
    Samsung?” and get a clear side-by-side comparison
    with prices and key specs from your own catalogue.
  • Store Knowledge Base — Reads your shipping, returns, contact,
    and about pages to answer policy questions accurately and
    dynamically — no hardcoded answers that break for other stores.
  • Conversation Context — Remembers context within a session so
    follow-up questions (“does it come in blue?”) work naturally.
  • Amazon Affiliate Fallback — When a product is out of stock,
    optionally suggest an Amazon affiliate link so you still earn a
    commission.

Live Human Chat

  • Human Handoff — When a customer types phrases like “I want
    to talk to a human”, “customer service”, “live agent”, or dozens
    of natural variants, the plugin detects the request and connects
    them to a real person on your team.
  • Admin Live Chats Dashboard — A dedicated Live Chats screen
    in your WordPress admin shows all active, waiting, and closed
    conversations in a two-panel interface. Keep the tab open to stay
    marked online for visitors.
  • Visitor Name Prompt — Before connecting, the visitor is
    optionally asked for their name. If skipped, they are identified
    as “Visitor #ID” so you can tell conversations apart.
  • Full Conversation Context for Agents — When a customer is
    handed off, the admin sees the complete prior AI conversation so
    there is no need to ask “how can I help?” twice.
  • Visitor Presence Dot — A green dot shows the visitor is
    active. It turns grey within 30 seconds if they close the tab.
  • Two-Tier Timeout — If your team does not respond within
    90 seconds, the visitor sees a friendly patience message. After
    5 minutes of no reply, the chat gracefully falls back to the AI
    assistant with an optional email capture.
  • Intelligent Offline Handling — When no admin is online the AI
    keeps helping. Visitors can optionally leave their email for a
    follow-up. Leads appear in the admin Live Chats list with a
    dedicated Leads section and unread badge.
  • Session Management — Close chats when resolved, or delete
    them permanently. Closed and lead sessions stay visible in
    their own sections until manually removed.
  • Zero External Dependencies — Live chat runs entirely within
    your WordPress site using secure AJAX polling over the REST API.
    No Pusher, no third-party service, no extra cost.
  • Email Notifications — Get an email when a customer starts a
    live chat or leaves their contact details while you are offline.

Privacy & Security

  • All live chat data is stored in your own WordPress database.
    Nothing is sent to an external service.
  • Session tokens are 32-character cryptographically random strings
    — not sequential IDs — so sessions cannot be enumerated.
  • All endpoints enforce nonces, capability checks, input
    sanitization, output escaping, and rate limiting.
  • Message content is sanitized server-side, and rich chat HTML
    (product cards, links, images) is additionally sanitized
    client-side via a bundled copy of DOMPurify before being
    rendered — see “Bundled Libraries” below.

Bundled Libraries

  • DOMPurify 3.1.6 — client-side HTML sanitizer, used to safely
    render rich chat content (product cards, links, images).
    Vendored locally at assets/js/vendor/purify.min.js; not loaded
    from a CDN. © Cure53 and other contributors. Dual-licensed under
    the Apache License 2.0 and Mozilla Public License 2.0, both
    GPL-compatible. github.com/cure53/DOMPurify

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.2 or later
  • WooCommerce 7.0 or later (must be installed and active)
  • PHP 7.4 or later
  • An API key from Groq, OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google (optional —
    Basic AI and Live Chat both work without one)

Support

  • Support Forum: wordpress.org/support/plugin/winaltchat-for-woocommerce
  • Email: support@winalttechnologies.com

We aim to respond to all support requests within 48 hours.

External Services

This plugin connects to third-party AI providers only when you
configure an external AI mode and enter your own API key. In Basic
AI mode and during live human chat, no external AI service is used.

AI Providers (optional — only when an API key is configured)

Customer messages, recent conversation context, and relevant store
and product context are sent to the AI provider you select so it
can generate a response. No data is sent to these providers when
using Basic AI mode.

  • Groq — groq.com | Privacy Policy | Terms of Service
  • OpenAI — openai.com | Privacy Policy | Terms of Use
  • Anthropic Claude — anthropic.com | Privacy Policy | Terms of Service
  • Google Gemini — ai.google.dev | Privacy Policy | Terms of Service

Amazon Associate Program (optional — only when a tag is configured)

When the Amazon fallback is enabled and no matching product is
found in your store, the plugin generates an Amazon search link
with your Associate tag. No customer data is transmitted to Amazon
by the plugin — the link simply directs the visitor’s browser.

  • Amazon — amazon.com | Privacy Notice

Deactivation Feedback (optional — only sent if you respond to the deactivation survey)

When you deactivate this plugin, an optional short survey asks why.
If you respond (or skip), your site URL, the plugin/WordPress/PHP
version, and whatever you entered in the survey are sent to
Winalt Technologies to help improve the plugin. No personal data is
collected beyond this unless you choose to type it into the free-text
field yourself.

  • Winalt Technologies — aisalesmanchatpro.com | Privacy Policy

Anonymous Usage Tracking (optional — off by default, only sent if you click “Allow”)

On first use, a notice asks permission to send anonymous “still
active” pings to help us understand real-world installs. Nothing is
sent unless you click “Allow” — you can also decline, or change your
choice later from the plugin’s General Settings tab. When enabled,
your site URL and the plugin/WordPress/PHP version are sent to Winalt
Technologies once immediately and then roughly once a day for as long
as it stays enabled. No personal or customer data is ever included.

  • Winalt Technologies — aisalesmanchatpro.com | Privacy Policy
